scenario: Bought 1 Jul 2024 for 12,000, sold 1 Jul 2025 for 9,000; insurance 1 Oct 2024 to 30 Sep 2025 for 730, so 91 days of cover run past the sale
derivation: Spec 7.7: period 1 Jul 2024 to 1 Jul 2025 (both inclusive). Running = fuel 500 (1 Nov 2024) + the insurance document counted whole on its ledger date, its start 1 Oct 2024, which is in the period = 730; so running = 500 + 730 = 1,230 over 2 entries. Depreciation 12,000 - 9,000 = 3,000 over exactly 12 months = 3,000 a year. Total 4,230.
Per month: the period touches 13 calendar months (Jul 2024 to Jul 2025): 1,230 / 13 = 94.615; plus 3,000 / 12 = 250; 344.615.

Spec 7.35 (decided 2026-10-28, #564): the insurance is 365 days (1 Oct 2024 to 30 Sep 2025) at 730, so 2 a day. The days up to and including the sale (1 Oct 2024 to 1 Jul 2025) are 92 + 182 = 274 days: 2024 = 92 days = 184, 2025 = 182 days = 364. The 91 days from 2 Jul to 30 Sep 2025 (182) are outside the ownership and fall in no year.
So the years' insurance is 184 + 364 = 548 and since bought's 730: the years add up to 182 less, exactly the outside days' share (91 x 2).

Years' depreciation, a straight line 12,000 to 9,000 over 365 days: 2024 from 1 Jul to the end of 31 Dec = 184 days = 3,000 x 184 / 365 = 1,512.329; 2025 to 1 Jul = 181 days = 1,487.671 (they add up to 3,000).

page: Total: £1,230.00 of running costs + £3,000.00 of depreciation = £4,230.00.
